description:
This Transformation Office role is the technical translator between business needs and the Business Systems and Data teams. The analyst takes a business need, works out what the systems and data must do, and writes requirements clear enough for an admin, developer, data engineer, or implementation partner to build without a second meeting. The role has a solid line to the Chief Transformation Officer and a dotted line to the VP of Business Systems and the VP of Data. It is a hands-on analyst seat, not a project-coordination seat. The first assignment is the pricing and packaging transformation, which covers quoting, entitlements, usage, and billing. The role partners on, but does not own, the Business Systems roadmap, release calendar, environment strategy, or SI contracts.

Expected Duties

  • Lead discovery with business owners, interviewing and observing the work to find the real requirement.

  • Author BRDs, system requirements, user stories with acceptance criteria, data mappings, and integration specs that engineers can build from directly.

  • Storyboard and wireframe future-state experiences, including screens, flows, decision points, and handoffs.

  • Document current- and future-state process flows and system diagrams across Salesforce, the product catalog and entitlements, NetSuite, and the data platform.

  • Frame solution options with trade-offs: configuration vs. custom, buy vs. build, where data should live, and SOX control implications.

  • Partner with admins, architects, data engineers, and developers to make sure designs are buildable, scalable, and compliant.

  • Own intake for cross-functional systems and data demand, including triage, sizing, and communication on what is in, what is next, and why.

  • Maintain one priority board for Business Systems and Data work in Asana (portfolio view) and Jira (delivery view), kept in sync.

  • Run regular prioritization reviews with Business Systems, Data, and functional stakeholders using enterprise prioritization frameworks.

  • Facilitate refinement, sprint planning, reviews, and retrospectives for the work in the pipeline.

  • Surface risks and dependencies early with options, and escalate when leadership intervention is needed.

  • Track milestones and status for Business Systems and Data initiatives in the enterprise portfolio view.

  • Define the test strategy, write test scenarios from acceptance criteria, coordinate UAT with business owners, and run go/no-go quality gates.

  • Support the Business Systems release calendar and change control with ready, tested, documented work.

  • Report delivery health across both teams: cycle time, on-time rate, defects, and throughput.

  • Use AI tools (Claude) to draft and refine requirements, user stories, storyboards, test cases, and status reporting; automate intake triage and backlog hygiene.

  • Champion AI adoption in analysis and delivery workflows and measure the productivity gains.

Qualifications

  • About 7 years as a technical business analyst, business systems analyst, or solutions analyst on enterprise SaaS platforms.

  • 3+ years facilitating agile delivery. Scrum master or delivery lead experience is a plus, not the core requirement.

  • A portfolio of requirements artifacts the candidate can walk through: BRDs or SRDs, process storyboards or wireframes, data mappings, and integration specs.

  • Experience analyzing both application and data needs, such as CRM or ERP enhancements alongside warehouse, master-data, or reporting deliverables.

  • Hands-on experience with Salesforce, ideally including CPQ or Revenue Cloud, and at least one billing or ERP platform (NetSuite preferred). Able to read a data model and an object schema.

  • Experience delivering quote-to-cash or lead-to-cash initiatives end to end.

  • Daily, practical use of AI tools in analysis and delivery work.

  • Nice to have: Salesforce Business Analyst or Administrator certification; CSM, PSM, or SAFe certification; IIBA CBAP or CCBA; experience with SI-led implementations or billing system selection; fintech or regulated-industry SaaS; SOX-controlled environments; exposure to Databricks, Sigma, or enterprise data governance.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Technical enough to debate data models, integrations (Boomi, Informatica, or similar), API contracts, and configuration vs. custom trade-offs with engineers, and to recognize when no build is needed.

  • Able to lead discovery through interviews and observation.

  • Fluent in Jira and Asana administration and reporting.

  • Comfortable with process and wireframing tools such as Lucid, Figma, or Miro.

  • Works transparently and decisively: discusses, then commits, and speaks with one voice on priorities.
